p: The hedge maze is one of the big crowd-pleasers. It's made from thousands of yew trees, and the reward for reaching the middle is a secret: an underground grotto, decorated with shells and mythical creatures, that leads you back out. It's a proper adventure for kids and a fun challenge for grown-ups.

Then there's something you won't find at any other castle: a museum of dog collars. It's a quirky collection spanning several centuries, from fearsome spiked collars designed to protect hunting dogs to fancy decorated ones. It's an oddity, but a charming one.

Out in the grounds, keep an eye out for the black swans gliding on the moat, a favourite with visitors. The Culpeper Garden is a lovely cottage-style garden bursting with colour in summer, and there's plenty of open space for a picnic by the water. Little ones will make a beeline for the play areas.
Give yourself a full day here, especially with kids. The grounds are big, so wear comfortable shoes, and check what events are on before you go, as the castle hosts all sorts through the year.

Afterwards, Maidstone is just a short drive away, with shops and places to eat by the River Medway. Or head out into the Kent countryside, with its villages, pubs and views across the North Downs, for a peaceful end to the day.
